Subject: Private deployment: MSA annex + evidence scope — next steps

Hi Stephanie / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo on Monday. Our legal and security teams reviewed the high level deck and have three primary asks before procurement will sign:

1) Clarify license scope for an on-prem/private deployment (operator vs. customer-managed operator) — specifically whether Operator credentials are required or whether a snapshot/VM transfer is acceptable.
2) Evidence & audit window: we need an agreed checklist of artifacts (logs, snapshot hashes, attestation letter) and a proposed cadence for handing over evidence.
3) Escrow-like contingency: in the event Redwood is unavailable, what is the uplift/transfer process (and who holds the keys)? Not looking for formal escrow right now but a workable mechanism.

I attached our internal requirements (Acme_legal_requirements.pdf). Can you propose a realistic timeline for legal review and provide an initial set of redlines we can send to our counsel? We are targeting an internal procurement cutoff of 2027-01-12.

Best,
Marta Lima
Head of Procurement (Acme Health)

Marta — thank you, this is clear and helpful. Attaching a short governance checklist and a proposed annex outline (privdeploy-governance-checklist_v1.docx).

Proposed approach:
- We will produce an MSA Annex (license & deployment rights) + an Order Form note that includes the SLA carve-outs for private deployments.
- For evidence, we suggest a two-track option: (A) Operator access limited to named personnel with ephemeral credentials + attestation, or (B) periodic snapshot deliveries (encrypted) with a signed handover protocol. We can map both to your requirements in the checklist.
- For contingency/escrow-like posture: we can offer a snapshot-handback + cryptographic proof-of-possession flow and an operator-runbook handover; true escrow (third-party escrow agent) is a separate procurement ask and we can scope cost.

Timeline we propose: initial redlines delivered by 2026-12-15, internal Redwood legal review by 2026-12-20, counterparty review requested by 2027-01-06. Does that fit your procurement schedule?

Next steps: please confirm whether Acme prefers operator access (option A) or snapshot transfer (option B) as the default; we'll mark the preferred option in the annex and include a fallback.

Thanks — looping in Marcus for technical constraints.

Stephanie / Lauren,

Quick notes from infra/security POV: happy to support both options but tradeoffs below — include these as clauses in the annex.

Option A — Limited Operator Access (ephemeral):
- Pros: fastest time to value, minimal data transfer.
- Cons: requires named operator list, background checks if customer insists, access logging and attestation required.
- Suggested contract text: access limited to "Designated Redwood operators" for incident response; access requires 48-hour notice except under agreed emergency conditions; all access logged and we will provide redacted logs on request.

Option B — Snapshot Transfer (recommended if Acme prefers no third-party operator):
- Pros: customer retains control of runtime; snapshot is encrypted and delivered with signed hash.
- Cons: larger upfront ops cost; longer lead time for restores and validation; requires a secure transfer mechanism and shared KMS or wrapped key.
- Suggested contract text: snapshot handover includes (i) SHA-256 hash signed by Redwood, (ii) transfer via SFTP/secure courier per SCP in the order form, (iii) 30-day verification window for the customer to validate.

Contingency / Escrow-like flow:
- We can offer a "snapshot escrow lite": quarterly encrypted snapshots stored with a mutually approved custodian (or customer-provided S3) plus attestation letter. Full third-party escrow will require procurement uplift; we can add budget language.

SLA carve-outs: list maintenance windows up front, define operator involvement windows and expected RTO for restore scenarios (we propose RTO of 72 hours for snapshot-based restores, lower for operator-assisted restores depending on connectivity).

I'll draft suggested contract language (2-3 paragraphs per option) and share by 2026-12-15.

—Marcus Lin
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

Marta — thanks for the patience. Per the team discussion we propose the following path and attached redlines (MSA_annex_privdeploy_v2_redlines.docx):

1) Default model: Snapshot Transfer (Option B) — encrypted snapshot delivery with signed SHA-256 hash and 30-day verification window.
2) Operator Access: available as a documented fall-back for incident response; requires explicit approval and a named-operator addendum.
3) Contingency / "escrow-lite": quarterly encrypted snapshot retention with customer-owned S3 or mutually approved custodian; add explicit budget language in Order Form if Acme requests full third-party escrow.
4) SLA carve-outs: maintenance windows and operator-assisted restore RTOs are called out in the Order Form; we propose an RTO of 72 hours for snapshot restores.

Next steps:
- Please review the attached redlines and confirm (A) preferred default (we set to snapshot), (B) acceptance of the 30-day verification window, and (C) whether you want Redwood to propose a custodian or use an Acme-provided storage bucket.
- If those are OK, we'll circulate a clean MSA Annex + Order Form and prep a DocuSign route for signature. Our target for counterparty legal comments is 2027-01-06 to keep procurement on your Jan 12 runway.
